para.text: For the development of XYGRAPH I followed some principles that are largely based on my own experience (so you do not have to agree with them).

para.style: text-align:left; text-indent:0px; margin-top:0px; margin-right:0px; margin-bottom:0px; margin-left:0px; line-height:1.00; background-color:transparent; white-space:normal; page-break-inside:auto; page-break-after:auto; border:none; tabstops:265px left ;

text-align:left; text-indent:0px; margin-top:0px; margin-right:0px; margin-bottom:0px; margin-left:0px; line-height:1.00; background-color:transparent; white-space:normal; page-break-inside:auto; page-break-after:auto; border:none; tabstops:265px left ;
para.text: One is that it has little use to construct an image on the screen if you cannot export it or save it in some way: the image gets lost when you shut down the computer.

para.style: text-align:left; text-indent:0px; margin-top:0px; margin-right:0px; margin-bottom:0px; margin-left:0px; line-height:1.00; background-color:transparent; white-space:normal; page-break-inside:auto; page-break-after:auto; border:none; tabstops:265px left ;
para.text: Of course you can always make a hardcopy of the screen but that is very rude.

para.style: text-align:left; text-indent:0px; margin-top:0px; margin-right:0px; margin-bottom:0px; margin-left:0px; line-height:1.00; background-color:transparent; white-space:normal; page-break-inside:auto; page-break-after:auto; border:none; tabstops:265px left ;
para.text: As XYGRAPH is to be used to construct graphs and diagrams that are basically vector-oriented, the obvious way is to create metafiles. However this limits XYGRAPH to the use of high-level procedures that have metafile equivalents.

para.style: text-align:left; text-indent:0px; margin-top:0px; margin-right:0px; margin-bottom:0px; margin-left:0px; line-height:1.00; background-color:transparent; white-space:normal; page-break-inside:auto; page-break-after:auto; border:none; tabstops:265px left ;
para.text: Another way to export the graph is to make high-resolution prints. This however requires reconstruction of the graph in a higher resolution and that can be achieved simply if the graph is constructed on a

para.text: The second principle that it must be robust. This is a principle that I have learned to appreciate over the years, it is better to wait some time and be sure that you get the correct solution, than get a quick answer but not be sure if it is correct (this principle applies much to simulations). Delphi's predecessor Turbo Pascal was based on this principle: it used only well documented BIOS routines. The applications were slow but very robust, and they always worked on any computer.

para.style: text-align:left; text-indent:0px; margin-top:0px; margin-right:0px; margin-bottom:0px; margin-left:0px; line-height:1.00; background-color:transparent; white-space:normal; page-break-inside:auto; page-break-after:auto; border:none; tabstops:265px left ;

para.text: When developing applications with XYGRAPH you have to distinguish between static and dynamic information.

para.style: text-align:left; text-indent:0px; margin-top:0px; margin-right:0px; margin-bottom:0px; margin-left:0px; line-height:1.00; background-color:transparent; white-space:normal; page-break-inside:auto; page-break-after:auto; border:none; tabstops:265px left ;
para.text: Static information is all the information that create the final display. The final display is that what you want to store for future reference or want to export. This generally comprises the graph itself, the legend, text etc. This display should be constructed using XYGRAPH routines only, and preferably on a paintbox. Keep in mind that information created by other means than XYGRAPH routines can only be saved by creating a hardcopy of the screen.

para.style: text-align:left; text-indent:0px; margin-top:0px; margin-right:0px; margin-bottom:0px; margin-left:0px; line-height:1.00; background-color:transparent; white-space:normal; page-break-inside:auto; page-break-after:auto; border:none; tabstops:265px left ;
para.text: Dynamic information is information of temporarily character like the ruler, display of co-ordinates and so. This information can be constructed using any canvas routine or whatever fancy method you like.
